\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ستارة} (sitāra)}{ستارة (sitāra)}]{\ar{ستارة} (sitāra) — a curtain}

\label{lesson:AR-C127-sitara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a toy, then the Arabic for a fridge.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ستارة}}
\textbf{\ar{ستارة}} — \emph{sitāra} — \textquotedblleft{}a curtain\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ستارة}} (\emph{sitāra}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{s-t-r}, \textquotedblleft{}to veil, to cover\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Sitāra} is a thing that covers.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sitāra}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sitāra}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{sitāra}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a toy, then the Arabic for a fridge, then say \emph{sitāra} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{قفل} (qufl)}{قفل (qufl)}]{\ar{قفل} (qufl) — a lock}

\label{lesson:AR-C127-qifl}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a fridge, then the Arabic for a curtain.

\emph{Read it:} \textbf{\ar{قال}}

Which letter is the deep \emph{q}? (\textbf{\ar{ق}}, \emph{qāf}, two dots above.)
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{قفل}}
\textbf{\ar{قفل}} — \emph{qufl} — \textquotedblleft{}a lock\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{قفل}} (\emph{qufl}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{q-f-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to return; to lock\textquotedblright{} (Lane), and Lane lists \emph{qufl}, \textquotedblleft{}a lock\textquotedblright{}, under it. The same root gives \emph{qāfila}, \textquotedblleft{}a caravan\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a fridge, then the Arabic for a curtain, then say \emph{qufl} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{منديل} (mindīl)}{منديل (mindīl)}]{\ar{منديل} (mindīl) — a handkerchief}

\label{lesson:AR-C127-mindil}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a curtain, then the Arabic for a lock.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{منديل}}
\textbf{\ar{منديل}} — \emph{mindīl} — \textquotedblleft{}a handkerchief\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{منديل}} (\emph{mindīl}) is usually traced to Greek \emph{mandilion}, \textquotedblleft{}towel, napkin\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from Latin \emph{mantēle}; Arabic grammarians placed it under \emph{n-d-l}.
\end{cousinweb}
